newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle close sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle close sharply higher.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures closed sharply higher despite late profit taking as futures took cues from higher cash cattle prices, traders said.

Live cattle settled 1.350 to 0.300 cent per lb higher with April up most at 68.525 cents. Feeder cattle ended 1.275 to 0.375 higher with May up most at 71.150 cents. May was briefly up the 1.500 cent limit while April and distant March posting new contract highs.
Increased fed cattle sales at higher prices Wednesday, active boxed beef sales again Thursday, weather concerns and a strong stopper for April certificates prompted the demand, traders said.

Packers paid $1 higher for fed cattle in southern and central Plains feedlots at the same time beef sales totaled nearly 400 loads early Wednesday. With beef sales running over 400 loads the past two days, there was growing speculation packers interest in fed cattle would be heightened.

"Trade will now think the packer will be cleaning out the coolers and that could mean they will get a little more aggressive" in buying fed cattle, said Dave Maher, livestock analyst for Securities Corporation of Iowa.
Poor weather in the Plains and Midwest and moderate fed cattle supplies expected into May added to strength, they said.
"We are not going to get into the larger (fed) numbers for a couple of more weeks," said Karl Skold, director of research for Frontier Risk Management.

Fund short covering added to demand from R.J. O'Brien and RBH to keep April strong late, traders said. Cargill Investor Services and ADM Investor Services bought June while RBH, LFG and locals sold, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, Term Commodities sold December 72 calls early. Commercials bought the June 74 straddle and sold June 61 and 62 puts. They also bought June 70 calls late, pit sources added.

May feeder cattle surged the daily limit as demand from falling corn futures, strong replacement interest and concern over possible calf death losses from recent storms in the northern Plains sparked buying which touched off buy stops, traders said.

"A tremendous amount of calves have been lost up there (North Dakota) and I'm still hearing that feedlots have empty pens" in the south, said Jim Clarkson, analyst for A and A Inc. "I'm hearing lots in Kansas and Texas are looking for the heavier weight feeders and there is not a steady supply of them - they're keeping them out on the wheat pasture longer."
Pastures are very good this year, Clarkson added.
E.D.& F. Man actively bought May before selling my Refco pared the limit advance. Iowa also bought with Cargill Investor Services a buyer at the close, pit sources said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.14 at $71.08 per cwt.
